```{r blind-switch}
UNBLIND <- as.logical(Sys.getenv("UNBLIND_STUDY3", "FALSE"))
# The blind switch, as in Study3_01_Quant.Rmd. While UNBLIND is FALSE this
# file reads the blind long data file, shuffles its labels again and shuffles
# the ratings right after the ratings are built (section 2.1), and writes
# every output to a blind_run/ subfolder of the folder its real counterpart
# goes to.
if (is.na(UNBLIND)) stop("UNBLIND_STUDY3 must be TRUE or FALSE.")

# A blind report belongs in blind_run/, and an unblinded report beside this
# file. The knit: line in the header reads the same environment variable and
# sends the report to the right folder when the file is knitted with
# RStudio's Knit button. A call to rmarkdown::render() must pass
# output_dir = "blind_run" in a blind run and leave it out in an unblinded
# run. A run whose report would land in the wrong folder stops here, before
# anything is written. The folder is read from the settings render() is
# running with; a knit that does not go through render() is not checked.
render_output_dir <- function() {
  frame <- Find(function(e) exists("output_dir", envir = e, inherits = FALSE) &&
                  exists("knit_input", envir = e, inherits = FALSE),
                sys.frames())
  if (is.null(frame)) return(NULL)
  d <- get("output_dir", envir = frame)
  normalizePath(if (is.null(d)) "." else d, mustWork = FALSE)
}
report_dir <- render_output_dir()
if (!UNBLIND && !is.null(report_dir) && basename(report_dir) != "blind_run") {
  stop("A blind report must be written to blind_run/. Knit with the Knit ",
       "button, or run rmarkdown::render(\"Study3_03_Integration.Rmd\", ",
       "output_dir = \"blind_run\").")
}
if (UNBLIND && !is.null(report_dir) && basename(report_dir) == "blind_run") {
  stop("An unblinded report must not be written to blind_run/. Set the ",
       "environment variable UNBLIND_STUDY3 to TRUE before knitting, or run ",
       "rmarkdown::render(\"Study3_03_Integration.Rmd\") without output_dir.")
}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = TRUE,
                      fig.align = "center")
```

} else {

# 0. What this file does

`Study3_02_Text.ipynb` measured the 1,530 justifications without seeing the
condition, the stated time or the rating. This file joins those three back
onto the measures and runs:

1. the two text checks the Study 1 registration fixes for every study, on
   both ratings, as the Study 3 registration says (section 3): how well the
   words predict the rating and the source condition in participants left
   out of fitting, and whether participants under the AI label reuse their own
   words across images more than Human participants do, with Holm correction
   across the two ratings;
2. the exploratory items the registration names (section 4): comparisons
   built on the word lists, word pleasantness and concreteness from published
   ratings, topics found by a model given no labels, and the words that carry
   the rating prediction.

Each justification was written after its rating, so none is read as the
rating's cause. Everything in section 4 is exploratory description.

# 1. Setup

## 1.1 Packages

```{r packages}
# dplyr, tidyr, tibble and readr build and write the tables. lme4 and
# lmerTest fit the mixed models of section 4. glmnet fits the penalised
# regressions, and Matrix stores the word counts. The two registered checks
# come from the shared helper text_checks.R.

  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(tibble)
  library(readr)
  library(lme4)
  library(lmerTest)
})
```

## 1.3 Run record

```{r run-record}
# The run record stores the SHA-256 checksum of every input (a 64-character
# fingerprint of the file's exact bytes), deletes the previous run's manifest
# now and each output's previous copy before the chunk that writes it, and
# writes the manifest last.
run <- start_run_record(INPUTS,
                        file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_integration_run_manifest.csv"),
                        STUDY_DIR)
write_run_inputs(run, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_integration_run_inputs.csv"))
cat("Run identifier:", run$run_id, "\n")

# Each input must be the file its producing run recorded. The long data file
# is checked against the manifest of Study3_01_Quant.Rmd in the same mode,
# and the text tables against the notebook's manifest. A manifest on disk
# means its run reached the end.
if (!file.exists(QUANT_MANIFEST) || !file.exists(TEXT_MANIFEST)) {
  stop("A run manifest is missing. Knit Study3_01_Quant.Rmd in the same mode ",
       "and run Study3_02_Text.ipynb to the end first.")
}
quant_manifest <- read_csv(QUANT_MANIFEST, show_col_types = FALSE)
text_manifest  <- read_csv(TEXT_MANIFEST, show_col_types = FALSE)
recorded <- bind_rows(
  select(quant_manifest, file, sha256),
  select(text_manifest, file, sha256))
input_check <- tibble(input = names(INPUTS),
                      file  = relative_path(INPUTS, STUDY_DIR),
                      sha256 = run$inputs$sha256) %>%
  left_join(rename(recorded, recorded_sha256 = sha256), by = "file") %>%
  mutate(matches_its_manifest = sha256 == recorded_sha256)
print(as.data.frame(select(input_check, input, file, matches_its_manifest)))
if (!all(input_check$matches_its_manifest %in% TRUE)) {
  stop("Some input is not the file its producing run recorded.")
}
cat("The notebook measured", unique(text_manifest$input_file), "\n")
```

# 2. The ratings and the text tables

## 2.1 The ratings, and the blind shuffle

```{r ratings}
# One row per response: the participant, the image, the dimension, the
# rating (NA for the five unscored ratings), the source and the stated time.
long <- read_csv(INPUTS[["long_data"]], show_col_types = FALSE,
                 col_types = cols(.default = col_character(),
                                  stimulus_num = col_integer(),
                                  rating = col_integer(),
                                  k_points = col_integer()),
                 na = "")
ratings <- long %>% select(id, stimulus_id, dimension, rating, Type, time)
stopifnot(nrow(ratings) == 1530, !anyDuplicated(ratings[, KEY]),
          all(ratings$Type %in% TYPE_LEVELS), all(ratings$time %in% TIME_LEVELS))

# In a blind run the labels are shuffled here, after the ratings are built
# and before any summary or model, with the method and seed of
# Study3_01_Quant.Rmd: source across participants, stated time within each
# participant across that participant's images. The blind long data file
# already carries shuffled labels; shuffling them again here keeps this file
# blind whichever long data file it is given.
shuffle_time_within <- function(df, seed) {
  units <- distinct(df, id, stimulus_id, time)
  if (anyDuplicated(units[, c("id", "stimulus_id")]) > 0) {
    stop("Some image carries more than one stated time.")
  }
  units <- units[order(units$id, units$stimulus_id, method = "radix"), ]
  had_seed <- exists(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv(), inherits = FALSE)
  if (had_seed) old_seed <- get(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv())
  on.exit({
    if (had_seed) assign(".Random.seed", old_seed, envir = globalenv())
    else rm(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv())
  }, add = TRUE)
  set.seed(seed)
  rows_by_id <- split(seq_len(nrow(units)),
                      factor(units$id, levels = sort(unique(units$id), method = "radix")))
  new_time <- character(nrow(units))
  for (rows in rows_by_id) {
    new_time[rows] <- units$time[rows][sample.int(length(rows))]
  }
  units$time <- new_time
  out <- df
  key <- match(paste(out$id, out$stimulus_id), paste(units$id, units$stimulus_id))
  out$time <- units$time[key]
  out
}

# The rating carries no label to shuffle, so in a blind run it is shuffled
# itself. Within each question, the scored ratings are dealt again among the
# scored responses, and the five responses without a score keep none. Each
# question keeps its ratings and their spread, and every link between a
# rating and its participant, image, justification, source and stated time
# is cut. Without this step the parts of this file that relate the words to
# the rating alone, such as the rating-from-words check of section 3.1 and
# the lasso of section 4.4, would be real results. Responses are taken in
# byte order of their identifiers, and the random-number state is put back
# afterwards.
shuffle_rating_within_dimension <- function(df, seed) {
  ord <- order(df$dimension, df$id, df$stimulus_id, method = "radix")
  had_seed <- exists(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv(), inherits = FALSE)
  if (had_seed) old_seed <- get(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv())
  on.exit({
    if (had_seed) assign(".Random.seed", old_seed, envir = globalenv())
    else rm(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv())
  }, add = TRUE)
  set.seed(seed)
  out <- df
  for (dim in sort(unique(df$dimension), method = "radix")) {
    rows <- ord[df$dimension[ord] == dim & !is.na(df$rating[ord])]
    out$rating[rows] <- df$rating[rows][sample.int(length(rows))]
  }
  out
}

if (!UNBLIND) {
  n_scored <- sum(!is.na(ratings$rating))
  ratings <- blind_shuffle(ratings, "id", "Type", seed = SEED)
  ratings <- shuffle_time_within(ratings, seed = SEED)
  ratings <- shuffle_rating_within_dimension(ratings, seed = SEED)
  stopifnot(sum(!is.na(ratings$rating)) == n_scored)
  cat("Blind run: source labels shuffled across participants, stated-time",
      "labels shuffled within each participant, ratings shuffled within each",
      "question, seed", SEED, "\n")
}
ratings <- ratings %>%
  mutate(Type = factor(Type, levels = TYPE_LEVELS),
         time = factor(time, levels = TIME_LEVELS))
cat("Responses:", nrow(ratings), "| participants:", n_distinct(ratings$id),
    "| scored ratings:", sum(!is.na(ratings$rating)), "\n")
```

## 2.2 The text tables and their contract

```{r text-tables}
# Every text table must carry its agreed columns and none of the forbidden
# ones (the condition, the rating, the text). The readers in text_checks.R
# stop if one does.
measure_cols <- c("id", "stimulus_id", "stimulus_num", "stimulus_type",
                  "dimension", "n_words",
                  "says_detail", "says_time", "says_skill", "says_concept",
                  "says_prompt", "says_machine_made", "machine_made_reading",
                  "prior_exposure", "anchor_echo",
                  "detail_polarity", "time_polarity", "skill_polarity",
                  "concept_polarity")
TRUE_FALSE_FLAGS <- c("says_detail", "says_time", "says_skill", "says_concept",
                      "says_prompt", "says_machine_made", "anchor_echo")
measures <- read_csv(INPUTS[["measures"]], show_col_types = FALSE,
                     col_types = cols(.default = col_character(),
                                      stimulus_num = col_integer(),
                                      n_words = col_integer()))
check_text_table(measures, measure_cols, "The measures file")
for (f in TRUE_FALSE_FLAGS) {
  stopifnot(all(measures[[f]] %in% c("True", "False")))
  measures[[f]] <- measures[[f]] == "True"
}

wordcounts <- read_text_wordcounts(INPUTS[["wordcounts"]])
vocabulary <- read_text_vocabulary(INPUTS[["vocabulary"]])
tokens     <- read_text_tokens(INPUTS[["tokens"]])

affect <- read_csv(INPUTS[["affect"]], show_col_types = FALSE,
                   col_types = cols(id = col_character(), stimulus_id = col_character(),
                                    dimension = col_character(),
                                    n_content_words = col_integer(),
                                    n_vad_matched = col_integer(), valence = col_double(),
                                    arousal = col_double(), dominance = col_double(),
                                    n_conc_matched = col_integer(),
                                    concreteness = col_double()))
check_text_table(affect, c(KEY, "n_content_words", "n_vad_matched", "valence",
                           "arousal", "dominance", "n_conc_matched",
                           "concreteness"), "The affect file")
topics <- read_csv(INPUTS[["topics"]], show_col_types = FALSE,
                   col_types = cols(id = col_character(), stimulus_id = col_character(),
                                    dimension = col_character(), topic = col_integer(),
                                    weight = col_double()))
check_text_table(topics, c(KEY, "topic", "weight"), "The topic file")
topic_words <- read_csv(INPUTS[["topic_words"]], show_col_types = FALSE,
                        col_types = cols(dimension = col_character(),
                                         topic = col_integer(), rank = col_integer(),
                                         word = col_character(), weight = col_double()))
check_text_table(topic_words, c("dimension", "topic", "rank", "word", "weight"),
                 "The topic word list")

# Every table keyed by response names exactly the responses of the ratings.
response_keys <- function(df) sort(unique(paste(df$id, df$stimulus_id, df$dimension)))
rating_keys <- response_keys(ratings)
for (nm in c("measures", "tokens", "affect", "topics")) {
  stopifnot(identical(response_keys(get(nm)), rating_keys))
}
cat("Every table keyed by response names the same", length(rating_keys),
    "responses as the ratings.\n")
```

## 2.3 Joining the flags to the ratings and the condition

```{r join}
# The measures were computed without the condition, the stated time or the
# rating. They are joined back here on the participant, the image and the
# dimension, one row to one row.
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_text_join_check.csv"))
joined <- measures %>%
  inner_join(ratings, by = KEY, relationship = "one-to-one")
join_check <- tibble(
  rows_in_measures = nrow(measures),
  rows_in_ratings  = nrow(ratings),
  rows_joined      = nrow(joined),
  only_in_measures = nrow(anti_join(measures, ratings, by = KEY)),
  only_in_ratings  = nrow(anti_join(ratings, measures, by = KEY)))
print(as.data.frame(join_check))
stopifnot(join_check$rows_joined == 1530, join_check$only_in_measures == 0,
          join_check$only_in_ratings == 0)
write_csv(join_check, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_text_join_check.csv"))
```

# 3. The two registered text checks

## 3.1 How closely the words track the rating and the condition

```{r recoverability}
# The first check asks how well the words alone predict the rating, and how
# well they predict the source condition, in participants left out of
# fitting. The model is ridge regression (a regression that shrinks each
# word's weight toward zero), scored on ten folds grouped by participant, so
# no participant is on both the fitting and the scoring side. For the
# condition the score is the AUC (the probability that a randomly chosen AI
# response gets a higher predicted probability of the AI condition than a
# randomly chosen Human response; one half is chance). The reference for
# each score is a permutation null, the same pipeline rerun on shuffled
# outcomes 200 times. Every setting is Study 1's, set as the defaults of
# text_recoverability(), and the reading rule is recoverability_readings().
# The check is descriptive and enters no correction family.
run_clear_outputs(run,
                  file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_text_wordcount_check.csv"),
                  file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_text_recoverability.csv"),
                  file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_text_recoverability_readings.csv"))

wordcount_check <- check_text_wordcounts(ratings, wordcounts, vocabulary)
print(as.data.frame(wordcount_check))
write_csv(wordcount_check, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_text_wordcount_check.csv"))

recover <- text_recoverability(ratings, wordcounts, dims = DIMS)
recover_readings <- recoverability_readings(recover)
write_csv(recover, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_text_recoverability.csv"))
write_csv(recover_readings,
          file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_text_recoverability_readings.csv"))
print(as.data.frame(select(recover, dimension, target, predictors, estimate,
                           ci_low, ci_high, null_95th, status)), digits = 3)
print(as.data.frame(select(recover_readings, dimension, target, predictors,
                           reading)))
```

## 3.2 Within-person word overlap by condition

```{r self-overlap}
# The second check predicts that participants under the AI label reuse their
# own words across images more than Human participants do, relative to
# others writing about the same image. For each participant and rating, the
# own-word overlap is the mean Jaccard overlap (words two texts share divided
# by the words either uses) across that participant's justifications, and
# the stranger baseline is the overlap of each justification with other
# participants' justifications of the same image. Their difference is
# regressed on the condition with the mean number of words as a covariate.
# The interval comes from 2,000 resamples of participants within each
# condition, with the stranger baseline rebuilt in each, and the two ratings
# are corrected together by Holm. The reading is supported, opposite
# direction or inconclusive.
run_clear_outputs(run,
                  file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_text_selfsimilarity_by_arm.csv"),
                  file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_text_selfsimilarity_per_person.csv"))
overlap <- text_self_overlap(ratings, tokens, dims = DIMS)
write_csv(overlap$by_arm,
          file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_text_selfsimilarity_by_arm.csv"))
write_csv(overlap$per_person,
          file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_text_selfsimilarity_per_person.csv"))
print(as.data.frame(overlap$by_arm %>%
                      filter(role == "registered comparison") %>%
                      select(dimension, quantity, estimate, ci_lo, ci_hi,
                             p_raw, p_holm, reading, status)), digits = 3)
```

# 4. Exploratory description

Everything in this section is exploratory. It describes what participants
wrote after choosing their rating, and none of it tests a prediction.

## 4.1 Comparisons built on the word lists

```{r word-list-comparisons}
# For each of the eight Study 1 word lists, the share of justifications it
# flags, by source, stated time and dimension. The prior-exposure list is
# split into its two opposite readings: the writer says the work looks
# familiar (asserted) or says they have never seen anything like it
# (negated). Two comparisons per list and dimension follow, in percentage
# points: AI minus Human, pooled over stated time, and 100 hours minus under
# 1 hour, pooled over source. Each has a 95 percent interval from 2,000
# resamples of participants with replacement (a participant drawn twice
# contributes all their justifications twice). No p-value is computed.
run_clear_outputs(run,
                  file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_text_wordlist_prevalence.csv"),
                  file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_text_wordlist_comparisons.csv"))

INDICATORS <- c(TRUE_FALSE_FLAGS, "prior_exposure_asserted", "prior_exposure_negated")
flags <- joined %>%
  mutate(prior_exposure_asserted = prior_exposure == "asserted",
         prior_exposure_negated  = prior_exposure == "negated") %>%
  select(id, stimulus_id, dimension, Type, time, all_of(INDICATORS))

prevalence <- flags %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(INDICATORS), names_to = "word_list", values_to = "flagged") %>%
  group_by(dimension, word_list, Type, time) %>%
  summarise(responses = n(), flagged = sum(flagged),
            percent = 100 * flagged / responses, .groups = "drop")
write_csv(prevalence, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_text_wordlist_prevalence.csv"))

flag_differences <- function(d) {
  out <- c()
  for (dim in DIMS) {
    dd <- d[d$dimension == dim, , drop = FALSE]
    M  <- as.matrix(dd[, INDICATORS]) * 1
    share <- function(rows) colMeans(M[rows, , drop = FALSE])
    out <- c(out,
      setNames(100 * (share(dd$Type == "AI") - share(dd$Type == "Human")),
               paste(dim, INDICATORS, "AI minus Human, pooled over stated time", sep = "|")),
      setNames(100 * (share(dd$time == "100 hours") - share(dd$time == "under 1 hour")),
               paste(dim, INDICATORS, "100 hours minus under 1 hour, pooled over source", sep = "|")))
  }
  out
}
comparisons <- text_boot_by_participant(flags, flag_differences,
                                        B = TEXT_N_BOOT, seed = SEED) %>%
  separate(quantity, into = c("dimension", "word_list", "comparison"), sep = "\\|") %>%
  mutate(unit = "percentage points", seed = SEED)
write_csv(comparisons, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_text_wordlist_comparisons.csv"))
cat("Prevalence rows:", nrow(prevalence), "| comparison rows:", nrow(comparisons),
    "| replicates defined:", min(comparisons$n_valid), "of", TEXT_N_BOOT, "\n")
```

## 4.2 Word pleasantness and concreteness

```{r affect}
# Each justification's mean valence (how pleasant its words are, 1 to 9),
# arousal (how excited they make a reader, 1 to 9), dominance (how much in
# control they make a reader feel, 1 to 9) and concreteness (how much they
# refer to things that can be seen or touched, 1 to 5), from Warriner,
# Kuperman and Brysbaert (2013) and Brysbaert, Warriner and Kuperman (2014),
# as the notebook scored them. The model is Study 1's, per dimension and
# measure:
#
#   score ~ source x rating_c + (1 | participant) + (1 | image)
#
# where rating_c is the rating minus that dimension's mean rating, so the
# source coefficient (AI minus Human, the Human condition as the reference)
# is the difference at the average rating. The sixteen p-values of the two
# coefficients are corrected by Benjamini-Hochberg, which holds the expected
# share of false positives among the rows called positive.
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_text_affect_by_arm.csv"))

rating_centres <- ratings %>% group_by(dimension) %>%
  summarise(rating_centre = mean(rating, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
scored <- ratings %>% filter(!is.na(rating)) %>%
  left_join(rating_centres, by = "dimension") %>%
  mutate(rating_c = rating - rating_centre)

AFFECT_MEASURES <- c("valence", "arousal", "dominance", "concreteness")
AFFECT_TERMS <- c(
  "TypeAI"          = "source difference (AI minus Human) at the average rating",
  "TypeAI:rating_c" = "source by rating interaction (AI minus Human, per rating point)")

fit_log <- list()
tidy_terms <- function(res, terms) {
  if (res$status$fit_error) {
    return(tibble(term = terms, estimate = NA_real_, std_error = NA_real_,
                  df = NA_real_, t = NA_real_, p_raw = NA_real_))
  }
  co <- summary(res$fit)$coefficients
  tibble(term = terms, estimate = co[terms, "Estimate"],
         std_error = co[terms, "Std. Error"], df = co[terms, "df"],
         t = co[terms, "t value"],
         p_raw = na_unless_usable(co[terms, "Pr(>|t|)"], res$status))
}

affect_rows <- list()
for (dim in DIMS) {
  for (m in AFFECT_MEASURES) {
    d <- affect %>% filter(dimension == dim, !is.na(.data[[m]])) %>%
      inner_join(scored, by = KEY) %>%
      mutate(score = .data[[m]])
    res <- fit_with_status(lmerTest::lmer(
      score ~ Type * rating_c + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id), data = d,
      REML = TRUE, control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")))
    step <- paste0("4.2 ", m, " ~ source x rating, ", dim)
    fit_log[[step]] <- res$status %>% mutate(step = step, dimension = dim, .before = 1)
    affect_rows[[step]] <- tidy_terms(res, names(AFFECT_TERMS)) %>%
      mutate(dimension = dim, measure = m, .before = 1) %>%
      mutate(quantity = unname(AFFECT_TERMS[term]),
             ci_lo = na_unless_usable(estimate - qt(0.975, df) * std_error, res$status),
             ci_hi = na_unless_usable(estimate + qt(0.975, df) * std_error, res$status),
             mean_Human = mean(d$score[d$Type == "Human"]),
             mean_AI    = mean(d$score[d$Type == "AI"]),
             n_scored   = nrow(d),
             n_participants = n_distinct(d$id),
             converged = res$status$converged, singular = res$status$singular,
             note = fit_note(res$status),
             model = paste0(m, " ~ Type * rating_c + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id), REML, bobyqa"))
  }
}
affect_by_arm <- bind_rows(affect_rows)
affect_by_arm <- affect_by_arm %>%
  mutate(p_bh = p.adjust(p_raw, method = "BH", n = nrow(affect_by_arm)),
         .after = p_raw)
write_csv(affect_by_arm, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_text_affect_by_arm.csv"))
print(as.data.frame(select(affect_by_arm, dimension, measure, term, estimate,
                           ci_lo, ci_hi, p_bh, converged, singular)), digits = 3)
```

## 4.3 Topics found by a model given no labels

```{r topics}
# The notebook fitted a topic model to each dimension without the condition
# or the rating, and gave each justification a weight on each topic, the
# weights summing to one. The model is Study 1's, per dimension and topic:
#
#   weight ~ source + rating_c + (1 | participant) + (1 | image)
#
# Topic weights are bounded and pile up at zero, so the source term is
# tested against a permutation null: the source labels are dealt again among
# the participants, each keeping one label, the model is refitted and the
# source term's t value is recorded, 200 times. The p-value is the share of
# shuffles, counting the observed data as one, whose t value is at least as
# far from zero as the observed one. The same 200 shuffles serve every topic
# of a dimension, and the p-values are corrected by Benjamini-Hochberg within
# each dimension. Each topic is labelled by its five heaviest words.
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_text_topics_by_arm.csv"))

N_TOPIC_PERM <- 200L
topic_labels <- topic_words %>% filter(rank <= 5) %>% arrange(dimension, topic, rank) %>%
  group_by(dimension, topic) %>%
  summarise(topic_label = paste(word, collapse = ", "), .groups = "drop")
topics_joined <- topics %>% filter(!is.na(weight)) %>%
  inner_join(scored, by = KEY)

# The source term's t value from one refit; a refit that fails gives NA and
# is counted.
topic_t <- function(d) {
  fit <- tryCatch(suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(
    lme4::lmer(weight ~ Type + rating_c + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id), data = d,
               REML = TRUE, control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")))),
    error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(fit)) return(NA_real_)
  co <- summary(fit)$coefficients
  if (!"TypeAI" %in% rownames(co)) NA_real_ else unname(co["TypeAI", "t value"])
}

topic_rows <- list()
for (dim in DIMS) {
  d_dim  <- topics_joined %>% filter(dimension == dim)
  id_arm <- distinct(d_dim, id, Type)
  id_arm <- id_arm[order(id_arm$id, method = "radix"), ]
  set.seed(SEED)
  shuffles <- replicate(N_TOPIC_PERM,
                        setNames(sample(as.character(id_arm$Type)), id_arm$id),
                        simplify = FALSE)
  for (k in sort(unique(d_dim$topic))) {
    d <- d_dim %>% filter(topic == k)
    res <- fit_with_status(lmerTest::lmer(
      weight ~ Type + rating_c + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id), data = d,
      REML = TRUE, control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")))
    step <- paste0("4.3 topic ", k, " weight ~ source + rating, ", dim)
    fit_log[[step]] <- res$status %>% mutate(step = step, dimension = dim, .before = 1)
    usable <- fit_usable(res$status)
    co <- if (res$status$fit_error) NULL else summary(res$fit)$coefficients
    t_obs <- if (is.null(co)) NA_real_ else unname(co["TypeAI", "t value"])
    t_null <- text_run_permutations(shuffles, function(lab) {
      dd <- d
      dd$Type <- factor(lab[dd$id], levels = TYPE_LEVELS)
      topic_t(dd)
    }, text_default_workers())
    n_valid <- sum(!is.na(t_null))
    topic_rows[[step]] <- tibble(
      dimension = dim, topic = k,
      quantity  = "source difference in topic weight (AI minus Human) at the same rating",
      estimate  = if (is.null(co)) NA_real_ else unname(co["TypeAI", "Estimate"]),
      std_error = if (usable) unname(co["TypeAI", "Std. Error"]) else NA_real_,
      t         = if (usable) t_obs else NA_real_,
      p_perm    = if (!usable || is.na(t_obs) || n_valid == 0) NA_real_ else
        (1 + sum(abs(t_null) >= abs(t_obs), na.rm = TRUE)) / (1 + n_valid),
      n_perm = N_TOPIC_PERM, n_perm_valid = n_valid, perm_seed = SEED,
      rating_estimate = if (is.null(co)) NA_real_ else unname(co["rating_c", "Estimate"]),
      mean_weight_Human = mean(d$weight[d$Type == "Human"]),
      mean_weight_AI    = mean(d$weight[d$Type == "AI"]),
      n_responses = nrow(d), n_participants = n_distinct(d$id),
      converged = res$status$converged, singular = res$status$singular,
      note = fit_note(res$status),
      model = "weight ~ Type + rating_c + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id), REML, bobyqa; source term tested against source labels shuffled across participants")
  }
}
topics_by_arm <- bind_rows(topic_rows) %>%
  group_by(dimension) %>%
  mutate(p_bh = p.adjust(p_perm, method = "BH", n = n()), .after = p_perm) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  left_join(topic_labels, by = c("dimension", "topic")) %>%
  relocate(topic_label, .after = topic)
write_csv(topics_by_arm, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_text_topics_by_arm.csv"))
print(as.data.frame(select(topics_by_arm, dimension, topic, topic_label, estimate,
                           p_perm, p_bh, n_perm_valid, converged, singular)),
      digits = 3)
```

## 4.4 The words that carry the rating prediction

```{r prediction-weights}
# Section 3.1 asks how well the words predict the rating, with ridge models
# that spread small weights over every word. This asks which words do the
# predicting, with the lasso, a penalised regression whose penalty sets most
# word weights to exactly zero, so only the words a prediction cannot do
# without keep one. As in Study 1, the penalty is chosen by ten-fold
# cross-validation grouped by participant, on the folds of section 3.1, with
# the vocabulary rebuilt inside each training fold by the five-response
# floor. The chosen penalty is lambda.1se, the strongest penalty whose
# cross-validated squared error is within one standard error of the best.
# The model is then refitted on every response at that penalty, and the
# words with a nonzero weight are reported with their signs. A weight is the
# change in the rating for one more use of the word, after the shrinkage.
# Among words that move together the lasso tends to keep one, so a word
# missing from the list may still go with the rating.
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_text_prediction_weights.csv"))

prepared <- prepare_text_ratings(ratings, "stimulus_id", "Type", TYPE_LEVELS)
wc_keyed <- wordcounts %>% mutate(.stim = stimulus_key(wordcounts, "stimulus_id"))

lasso_rating_weights <- function(dim) {
  fr     <- text_dimension_frame(prepared, wc_keyed, dim)
  resp   <- fr$resp
  counts <- fr$counts
  y      <- resp$rating

  set.seed(TEXT_SEED)
  outer_by_id <- text_participant_folds(fr$id_arm, TEXT_N_OUTER_FOLDS, TYPE_LEVELS)
  outer_fold  <- unname(outer_by_id[resp$id])

  vocab_all <- text_floor_vocabulary(resp, counts, rep(TRUE, nrow(resp)),
                                     TEXT_WORD_MIN_RESPONSES)
  X_all  <- text_response_word_matrix(resp, counts, vocab_all$word)
  fitted <- text_with_warnings(glmnet::glmnet(X_all, y, family = "gaussian", alpha = 1))
  full_fit <- fitted$value
  lam      <- full_fit$lambda
  warns    <- fitted$warnings

  fold_loss <- matrix(NA_real_, TEXT_N_OUTER_FOLDS, length(lam))
  fold_n    <- integer(TEXT_N_OUTER_FOLDS)
  for (k in seq_len(TEXT_N_OUTER_FOLDS)) {
    tr <- outer_fold != k
    Xk <- text_response_word_matrix(
      resp, counts,
      text_floor_vocabulary(resp, counts, tr, TEXT_WORD_MIN_RESPONSES)$word)
    fk <- text_with_warnings(glmnet::glmnet(Xk[tr, , drop = FALSE], y[tr],
                                            family = "gaussian", alpha = 1,
                                            lambda = lam))
    warns <- c(warns, fk$warnings)
    pk <- predict(fk$value, Xk[!tr, , drop = FALSE], s = lam)
    fold_loss[k, ] <- colMeans((as.matrix(pk) - y[!tr])^2)
    fold_n[k]      <- sum(!tr)
  }
  cvm  <- apply(fold_loss, 2, weighted.mean, w = fold_n)
  cvsd <- sqrt(apply(sweep(fold_loss, 2, cvm)^2, 2, weighted.mean, w = fold_n) /
                 (TEXT_N_OUTER_FOLDS - 1))
  i_min      <- which.min(cvm)
  lambda_1se <- max(lam[cvm <= cvm[i_min] + cvsd[i_min]])

  warns  <- unique(warns)
  status <- if (length(warns) == 0) "ok" else "nonconvergence"
  b <- as.matrix(coef(full_fit, s = lambda_1se))[, 1]
  b <- b[setdiff(names(b), "(Intercept)")]
  b <- b[b != 0]
  words_tbl <- if (length(b) == 0) {
    tibble(word = NA_character_, coefficient = NA_real_, sign = NA_character_,
           rank = NA_integer_, n_responses_word = NA_integer_)
  } else {
    tibble(word = names(b), coefficient = unname(b)) %>%
      mutate(sign = ifelse(coefficient > 0, "positive", "negative"),
             rank = as.integer(rank(-abs(coefficient), ties.method = "first"))) %>%
      left_join(rename(vocab_all, n_responses_word = n_responses), by = "word") %>%
      arrange(rank)
  }
  words_tbl %>%
    mutate(dimension = dim, target = "rating", predictors = "words", .before = 1) %>%
    mutate(lambda_1se = lambda_1se, lambda_min = lam[i_min],
           n_words_in_model = nrow(vocab_all), n_nonzero = length(b),
           cv_loss = "squared error", n_folds = TEXT_N_OUTER_FOLDS,
           seed = TEXT_SEED, n_responses = nrow(resp), status = status,
           note = if (length(warns) == 0) "status ok; no warning from any fit" else
             paste0("status nonconvergence; ", paste(warns, collapse = "; ")),
           model = paste0("lasso linear regression (glmnet, alpha = 1), rating on ",
                          "the word counts; penalty at lambda.1se from ten-fold ",
                          "cross-validation grouped by participant with the ",
                          "vocabulary rebuilt in each training fold; refitted ",
                          "on all responses"))
}

prediction_weights <- bind_rows(lapply(DIMS, lasso_rating_weights))
write_csv(prediction_weights, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_text_prediction_weights.csv"))
for (dim in DIMS) {
  pw <- filter(prediction_weights, dimension == dim)
  cat(dim, "(", pw$status[1], "):", pw$n_nonzero[1], "of", pw$n_words_in_model[1],
      "words keep a weight at lambda.1se\n")
}
```

# 5. Fit status

```{r fit-log}
# One row per step that fits a model: the mixed models of sections 4.2 and
# 4.3, and the two registered checks, which report their own status (ok,
# nonconvergence or error) from the warnings their fits raised.
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_text_fit_log.csv"))
fit_log_tbl <- bind_rows(
  bind_rows(fit_log) %>% mutate(kind = "linear mixed model",
                                usable = !fit_error & converged),
  recover %>% distinct(dimension, status, note) %>%
    transmute(step = "3.1 recoverability", dimension, kind = "ridge regressions",
              fit_error = status == "error", converged = status == "ok",
              singular = NA, lme4_messages = note, usable = status == "ok"),
  overlap$by_arm %>% filter(role == "registered comparison") %>%
    transmute(step = "3.2 within-person overlap", dimension,
              kind = "ordinary least squares", fit_error = status == "error",
              converged = status == "ok", singular = NA,
              lme4_messages = note, usable = status == "ok")
) %>% relocate(step, dimension, kind, usable)
print(as.data.frame(select(fit_log_tbl, step, usable, fit_error, converged, singular)))
write_csv(fit_log_tbl, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_text_fit_log.csv"))
```
